Identifies, manages, integrates and/or adapts resources to achieve project goals while effectively managing scope, schedule and budget for assigned projects. Prepares schedules for project completion, implementing a system for review, control, and reporting on project status and recommends which phases of the project will be performed in-house or by contract. Implements quality assurance processes to ensure all aspects of the project are handled in a professional manner, meet the agreed to customer needs, and are in compliance with all contracts let by Public Building Services, General Services Administration.

Negotiates and coordinates project plans, budget objectives and schedules with management of affected customer agencies to establish and/or manage customer expectations. Informs customer officials of project status and any requirements for additional agency initiated action.

Monitors action in support of project plans and schedules and reports deviations and problems to appropriate General Services Administration and other agency officials.
To evaluate your qualifications, your resume must clearly demonstrate how you meet the specialized experience described below. Your resume must not exceed two pages.

To ensure your qualifications can be fully evaluated, we recommend including the following information: Name, address, telephone number, email address; Job Title (if Federal Service, provide series and grade; if not in GS plan, provide GS equivalent grade); Relevant work experience—should include employer name, job title, start and end dates (month/year), the number of hours worked per week and descriptions that explain how you meet the required qualifications in the job announcement.

Education, certifications or licensures—If the job announcement requires any education, certifications or licensures, make sure to include the required information and any required documents like transcripts.

Your resume should contain enough information to make a valid determination that you fully meet experience requirements for each grade level you are applying to. If you do not provide enough information for us to determine your qualifications, you may be rated ineligible.

If you have volunteered your service through a National Service program (e.g., Peace Corps, Americorps), we encourage you to apply and include this experience on your resume. The GS-12 salary range starts at $89,508 per year.

If you are a new federal employee, your starting salary will likely be set at the Step 1 of the grade for which you are selected. To qualify, you must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 level or higher in the Federal service.

Specialized experience is defined as experience utilizing project management practices and tools to simultaneously manage multiple construction and/or repair and alteration projects in a real estate environment.

This experience must include: Managing projects (balancing scope/quality, schedule and budget) requiring the services of multiple disciplines (i.e., construction, design, IT, telecommunications, interior furnishings, etc.) from project initiation phase through financial closeout; Interpreting customer needs and developing them into actionable requirements; Developing, managing, and balancing project plans, budgets, and schedules; and Coordinating and facilitating decisions by managing multiple stakeholders.

Performing assigned duties in a manner that promotes quality health care, outstanding customer service, and the maintenance of an environment committed to serving Veterans. Manages and controls the use of data related to these programs regarding day-to-day functioning and program evaluation.

Plans, organizes, and directs administrative, operational, patient and personnel activities for the Well-Being Programs and/or the Services. Administers information and analytical systems to evaluate and enhance the quality of service provided to patients.

Develops and implements information systems to track service activities including visits, referrals, staff productivity, use of Whole Health specific measures, patient demographics, equipment utilization and patient satisfaction in concert with the Whole Health Leadership. Supervises a group of employees performing work at various GS levels (e.g.

Complementary and Integrative Health instructors, Whole Health Coaches, and Whole Health Partners) and provides administrative, technical and clinical supervision necessary for accomplishing the work of the unit/services including monitoring outreach efforts and for the management, coordination, planning, and development of key administrative activities for the Whole Health Program.

Performs the administrative and personnel management function relative to staff supervised. Formulates, interprets and implements policies and procedures for patient programs and the Whole Health Service, as appropriate.

Serves as a member of the Whole Health leadership team, and serves on other VA committees, focus groups, and administrative/clinical boards, representing Whole Health Service on special projects as deemed appropriate.

Responsible for submitting reports to the Clinical Director, Medical Center Supervisors/Managers and the Executive Leadership Team (ELT), as appropriate and advising management on issues, making recommendations in a timely manner for improvement in services. Performs other duties as assigned.

Work Schedule: Monday-Friday; 7:30am to 4:00pm or 8:00am to 4:30pm Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Functional Statement #: 10083F Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized
Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy.

Education and experience: The individual must meet at least one of the requirements below: (1) Bachelor's degree in Physical Therapy AND five (5) years of progressively independent experience as a physical therapist. (2) Master's degree in Physical Therapy AND two (2) years of progressively independent experience as a physical therapist.

(3) Doctorate degree in physical therapy. Licensure: Individuals hold a full, current, and unrestricted license to practice physical therapy in a State, Territory or Commonwealth of the United States, or in the District of Columbia.

Non-licensed PTs, who otherwise meet the basic requirements in this standard, may be given a temporary appointment as a graduate PT at the GS-11 grade level under the authority of 38 U.S.C. 7405 (a)(1)(D) for a period not-to-exceed two years from the date of employment on the condition that such PT provide care only under the supervision of a PT who is licensed.

Failure to obtain licensure during that period is justification for termination of the temporary appointment. Grade Determinations: GS- 13 Physical Therapist (Supervisory) Experience: In addition to meeting the basic requirements, one year of progressively complex experience equivalent to the GS-12 grade level.

In addition, the candidate must demonstrate all the following KSAs. Demonstrated Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: 1. Knowledge of contemporary physical therapy across multiple areas of practice, and the demonstrated ability to apply this knowledge to provide clinical guidance to Staff PTs within the department. 2.

Knowledge of human resources administration, including such functions as the ability to interview and select qualified applicants, monitor and evaluate performance, and maintain effective labor management relations within scope of responsibility. 3. Ability to effectively supervise, direct, and manage a physical therapy staff. 4.

Skill in forging positive interpersonal relationships and conflict resolution. 5. Ability to analyze clinically appropriate data effectively to optimize quality, performance, and productivity within the section. 6.

Ability to set priorities, delegate tasks, and solve problems in order to meet multiple deadlines and identify/address organizational problems. 7. Ability to manage advocacy roles and planning activities within the VA and the greater rehabilitation community.

Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/. The full performance level of this vacancy is GS-13. The actual grade at which an applicant may be selected for this vacancy is GS-13. Physical Requirements: See VA Directive and Handbook 5019.

Overview BerryDunn is seeking a Senior Consultant to join our Medicaid Practice Group .

As part our consulting team focused on state Medicaid agency clients, you’ll leverage your leadership and Medicaid program and policy skills along with drive, initiative, and problem-solving abilities to help Medicaid agencies improve the health and lives of individuals.

You’ll be the success partner for Medicaid agencies in building healthier communities and stronger futures.

You will leverage your Medicaid program and policy project management skills to help a current client by leading projects within a program of multiple Medicaid initiatives focused on waiver and state plan amendment design, development, and implementation at various stages in their project lifecycle.

You will be either remotely based or out of one of our several office locations. You will report to and partner with senior management in our Medicaid team both for client work and career development. With a growth mindset, you will mentor junior staff as well as drive your personal growth with the support of a learning and development culture.

Travel Expectations: Up to 50%.

You Will Use your knowledge and experience to provide project management, subject matter knowledge and leadership; this includes helping develop client deliverables such as program and policy recommendations, state plan and waiver amendments, complex analysis, ongoing status reports, data and technical strategy plans, and presentations.

Build relationships with project team members including client contacts, stakeholders, federal partners, and vendor contacts. You’ll also communicate project and delivery status to our clients, team members, and other stakeholders.

Oversee the work of junior colleagues and provide guidance around schedule, scope, and deliverable for team members reporting to you. Develop your own career plan and mentor BerryDunn team members through partnered practice, knowledge sharing, and collaborating on project deliverables.

Participate in marketing and business development activities, such as writing blog posts, attending conferences, reviewing Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and assisting with go/no-go decision-making.

You Have 5 years relevant professional experience in state or federal government, healthcare, and/or consulting Minimum of 3 years’ experience working directly for, or consulting directly with, a State Medicaid agency Significant experience working with the Medicaid program and policy, in one or more of the following areas: Developing and /or implementing Medicaid policy and programs Interpreting and analyzing federal laws and regulations, documenting recommendations for achieving compliance Supporting skills such as stakeholder engagement, research, and meeting facilitation Alternative experience working for managed care plans and/or state Medicaid managed care plans, or other relevant stakeholders Demonstrated experience with project management and problem solving for clients as well as using critical thinking skills to adapt to changing priorities in a deadline-focused environment Excellent written and verbal communication and client relationship building skills Bachelor’s degree or years of experience in substitution for a degree Compensation Details The base salary range targeted for this role is $100,000 - $115,000.

This salary range represents BerryDunn ’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting.

If an applicant possesses experience, education, or other qualifications more than the minimum requirements for this posting, that applicant is encouraged to apply, and a final salary range may then be based on those additional qualifications; compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, years of experience, depth of experience, seniority, merit, education, training, amount of travel, and other relevant business considerations.

Applicants applying for the GS-14 grade level must meet the following requirements: Have IT-related experience demonstrating EACH of the nine competencies AND one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 level in the Federal service as described below: IT SPECIALIST COMPETENCY REQUIREMENTS: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail.

Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services.

Decision Making - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change.

Information Management - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems.

Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations.

Oral Communication - This skill is generally demonstrated by assignments where the applicant persuades others to take a particular course of action or to accept findings, recommendations, changes, or alternative viewpoints.

Problem Solving - This skill is generally demonstrated by assignments where the applicant identifies and accommodates technology and resource constraints. Teamwork - Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals.

Technical Competence – Uses knowledge that is acquired through formal training or on-the-job experience to perform one's job; works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to the job; advises others on technical issues.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: Specialized experience is defined as: Managing staff that provide or support delivery of modern IT networking product(s), platform(s), or service(s); leading the overall planning, management, and direction of a program or of projects; and utilizing modern development and program methodologies, such as Agile iterative development, to manage product or service delivery.

The Agile Delivery Manager (ADM) is accountable for delivering business value across one or more agile teams, specifically in support of the organization’s digital transformation.

Acting as a servant leader and connector between strategic intent and operational execution, the ADM sits at the bridge point between the product/feature layer (Product Owners, Business Analysts, Business Owners) and the delivery layer (Engineering Managers, Developers, QA, and the Scrum Masters who own team-level performance).

The ADM ensures that delivery aligns with product roadmaps, value streams, and enterprise priorities.
This role is not about managing tasks—it’s about enabling flow, clarity, and measurable outcomes that advance the organization’s customer and business goals. The ADM owns the health and predictability of the Program Increment (PI): making sure it is planned well, tracked honestly, and delivered against — while escalating risks and dependencies before they become blockers. .

s.h: The role is responsible for the following results
s.t:
Delivery Flow and Value
Consistently leveraging lean and agile practices to achieve outcomes, not just complete output.
Orchestrate planning and coordination activities across multiple teams, including PI Planning, Scrum of Scrums and cross-team synchronization, and protecting the teams against interference and over commitment, to sustain focus and health velocity.
Advise Product Owners and Business Analysts in backlog management and sequencing to ensure clear cross-team prioritization.
Monitor flow and delivery health metrics (predictability, throughput, cycle time, PI objective achievement) and share them with teams to celebrate progress and surface improvement opportunities
Use performance and progress data to increase transparency and predictability in meeting commitments to the business.
Facilitate the adoption and evolution of agile practices to continuously improve how the organization produces high quality and high value outcomes.
Align teams with strategic goals through transparent sequencing of work, clear identification of cross-team dependencies; own the identification, tracking, and mitigation of delivery risks and issues, ensuring timely resolution or escalation.
Facilitate scaled/cross-team agile events (e.g., PI Planning, System Demo, Inspect & Adapt, Scrum of Scrums) so they are productive and time-boxed, setting a consistent standard of effectiveness across teams. Team-level ceremonies remain owned by Scrum Masters. Ensure delivery standards and definitions of done are applied consistently across the teams.
Enablement & Coaching
Coach Scrum Masters, Business Owners, Product Owners and Business Analysts to communicated in terms of value delivered rather than requirement fulfillment.
Guide continuous improvement through retrospectives, delivery health checks, and root-cause analysis at the multi-team and PI Levels
Build agile maturity through mentoring, modeling psychological safety, and reenforcing learning cycles.
Stakeholder Engagement
Translate delivery progress into business impact, reporting what value was realized, not just completed.
Own upward and outward communication of delivery status, risks, and PI outcomes to executives, business owners, the Governance & Transformation Lead, and technology leadership.
Ensure the “voice of delivery” is represented in strategic planning and portfolio discussions.

PI predictability (planned vs. delivered PI objectives) across teams in scope.
Flow metrics trend (cycle time, throughput, work-in-progress) shared and improving over time.
Time-to-resolution on escalated risks, issues, and cross-team dependencies.
Stakeholder-reported clarity and trust in delivery commitments (Business Owners, executive sponsors).
Team-reported psychological safety and agile maturity progression.

Grocery and Retail is a startup within Uber, focused on building the future of on-demand commerce. We power delivery across groceries, alcohol, convenience, pet, pharmacy, retail, and more-combining the speed and innovation of a startup with the scale of Uber's global platform.
Our commercial organization supports a diverse portfolio of merchants, ranging from strategic Enterprise partners to thousands of small and medium-sized businesses. Successfully serving both requires a combination of high-touch relationship management and scalable commercial programs.
We're looking for a Commercial Program Manager who will directly own a portfolio of Enterprise merchant relationships while also leading programs that improve how we support, engage, and grow our long-tail SMB business.

As a Commercial Program Manager, you will operate across two critical areas of our commercial organization: Enterprise Account Management and SMB Program Management.
You will directly manage a select portfolio of Enterprise merchants, owning the commercial relationship, business performance, and long-term growth strategy for those partners. You'll develop joint business plans, identify growth opportunities, lead business reviews, navigate operational challenges, and work cross-functionally to strengthen each partnership.
At the same time, you will lead programs designed to improve how Uber manages thousands of SMB merchants at scale. Rather than directly managing the SMB long tail, you'll build and optimize the programs, processes, segmentation strategies, reporting, automation, and commercial playbooks that enable Account Managers and Account Coordinators to effectively manage large books of business.
This role is ideal for someone who combines strong commercial and relationship-management skills with structured program management, analytical thinking, and operational problem solving. Success requires the ability to move seamlessly between strategic merchant conversations and building scalable solutions for a complex commercial organization.

Enterprise Account Management & Growth - 30%
Own a select portfolio of Enterprise merchant partners, serving as the primary commercial point of contact and trusted advisor.
Develop joint business plans focused on growing sales, improving operational performance, and strengthening long-term partnerships.
Identify and execute growth opportunities across promotions, advertising, merchandising, product adoption, and other commercial levers.
Lead regular business reviews using performance data and marketplace insights to identify opportunities and establish clear action plans.
Lead commercial conversations and negotiations while balancing merchant objectives with Uber's broader business priorities.
Partner cross-functionally across Operations, Product, Marketing, Sales, and other teams to resolve merchant challenges and unlock growth.
SMB Program Management & Commercial Strategy - 45%
Own programs that improve how Uber supports, engages, and grows thousands of long-tail SMB merchants.
Lead commercial initiatives from strategy through execution, defining objectives, workstreams, stakeholders, timelines, and success metrics.
Develop merchant segmentation and prioritization strategies that help commercial teams focus resources on the highest-impact opportunities.
Build programs across merchant growth, lifecycle management, demand generation, operational performance, inventory and catalog health, and merchant engagement.
Develop scalable engagement strategies that enable Account Managers and Account Coordinators to effectively manage large books of business.
Partner cross-functionally across Operations, Product, Strategy, Marketing, Sales, and Analytics to launch and scale SMB initiatives.
Process Improvement, Automation & Enablement - 15%
Identify recurring operational challenges across the SMB long tail and develop scalable solutions that improve commercial execution.
Standardize workflows, playbooks, and operating processes across large merchant portfolios.
Identify opportunities to automate repetitive or manual work and improve Account Manager and Account Coordinator productivity.
Build tools, playbooks, and resources that enable commercial teams to spend more time on high-value merchant engagement and growth.
Partner with Product and Engineering to advocate for tooling and product enhancements that improve scaled merchant management.
Data, Reporting & Commercial Insights - 10%
Use merchant and marketplace data to identify trends, segment opportunities, prioritize initiatives, and inform commercial strategy.
Develop reporting that provides visibility into merchant health, engagement, growth, and operational performance.
Establish success metrics for SMB programs and measure their impact on merchant and business outcomes.
Translate insights from Enterprise account management and SMB performance into clear recommendations for commercial leadership.

The Principal Project Manager is a senior delivery leader within Professional Services, responsible for the rigor, predictability, and outcomes of Cyara ’s implementation and services portfolio.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Professional Services, this is a player-coach role: you will personally own a portfolio of complex, strategic customer engagements while leading and developing a small team of Project Managers supporting customers across North America, EMEA, and APAC.

You will set the standard for how Professional Services plans, governs, reports on, and closes out customer projects — bringing PMO discipline to a global delivery organization.

Portfolio Leadership & Delivery Execution
Own a portfolio of complex, multi-phase, and strategic customer implementations and services engagements from initiation through formal completion and closure.
Lead and coach a small team of Project Managers, setting expectations, reviewing project plans, and holding the team accountable to consistent delivery standards.
Personally manage select high-value or high-complexity accounts, staying close to delivery while building the team’s ability to do the same.
Project Governance & PMO Standards
Establish consistent project-management standards, templates, and methodologies across Professional Services, covering planning, resource forecasting, effort estimation, and change control.
Define governance for complex, multi-phase, recurring, and long-duration programs, including clear criteria for closing individual phases and full projects instead of leaving them administratively open.
Build the risk management, dependency tracking, and executive escalation practices that keep engagements on track and stakeholders informed.
Cross-Functional Partnership & Executive Communication
Partner with Professional Services leadership, consultants, technical resources, Sales, and Customer Success to align delivery plans with customer commitments and business priorities.
Serve as the executive point of contact for project status, risk, and escalation on strategic accounts, communicating directly with customer sponsors and internal leadership.
Build feedback checkpoints at meaningful delivery milestones so customer satisfaction is measured throughout an engagement, not only at its conclusion.
Reporting, Financial Performance & Continuous Improvement
Own project health, milestone, budget, hours, and utilization reporting, using Rocketlane or a comparable PSA platform to give leadership real-time visibility into the portfolio.
Track forecast accuracy, time-to-value, and financial performance across the portfolio, and correct course when projects drift from plan.
Identify systemic delivery risks from portfolio data, recommend process changes, and build the playbooks, templates, and dashboards that let the PMO function scale.

Delivery Leadership & Project Management Experience
Significant experience managing complex enterprise technology implementations or Professional Services engagements, including multiple concurrent projects or portfolios.
Experience leading and developing Project Managers, with the ability and willingness to personally manage projects while also providing team leadership.
Strong executive customer communication and escalation-management skills, gained working directly with customer sponsors and internal leadership on complex engagements.
PMO & Project Management Discipline
Demonstrated ability to build or mature PMO processes: templates, governance standards, reporting, and delivery methodology.
Strong understanding of PMI-aligned project-management disciplines, including planning, risk, scope, and change management.
Experience managing project financials — budgets, hours, forecasts, and change requests — and resource plans across a portfolio of engagements.
Experience working across global, cross-functional organizations spanning multiple regions and time zones.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business, information technology, or a related field.

Experience with Rocketlane, Salesforce, or comparable PSA platforms preferred.
SaaS, enterprise software, CX, CCaaS, telecommunications, testing/automation, or related technology experience preferred.
Why This Role
You’ll bring PMO rigor to a global Professional Services organization, shaping how Cyara plans, governs, and closes customer engagements across North America, EMEA, and APAC.
You’ll operate as both a player and a coach — owning strategic accounts directly while building the standards and capability of a growing Project Management team.
You’ll report to the Senior Director, Professional Services, and partner closely with Professional Services leadership, Sales, and Customer Success to improve time-to-value, financial performance, and customer satisfaction across the portfolio.

Bloomreach is building the world’s premier agentic platform for personalization .We’re revolutionizing how businesses connect with their customers, building and deploying AI agents to personalize the entire customer journey.
We're taking autonomous search mainstream, making product discovery more intuitive and conversational for customers, and more profitable for businesses.
We’re making conversational shopping a reality, connecting every shopper with tailored guidance and product expertise — available on demand, at every touchpoint in their journey.
We're designing the future of autonomous marketing , taking the work out of workflows, and reclaiming the creative, strategic, and customer-first work marketers were always meant to do.
And we're building all of that on the intelligence of a single AI engine — Loomi — so that personalization isn't only autonomous…it's also consistent.From retail to financial services, hospitality to gaming, businesses use Bloomreach to drive higher growth and lasting loyalty. We power personalization for more than 1,400 global brands, including American Eagle, Sonepar, and Pandora.
Bloomreach builds agentic AI systems for our customers. We also run them ourselves.
Our AI SDR program books sales meetings with AI - inbound and outbound, across four regions, in multiple languages. The program needs an owner: someone who sets its direction, drives its results, and proves its ROI. This is a program leadership role, not an engineering one. Two dedicated AI ops experts build and run the platform.

You decide what it does, why, and for whom. You should understand AI agents well enough to direct the people building them - your leverage is judgment, but being tech savvy is a must.
The team experiments by default: we test new AI tools, run scoped POCs, and keep what works. You'll own the program, its direction, its results, its pipeline number.
What you'll own
The AI SDR program, end to end. Inbound and outbound, AMER + EMEA + APAC. Who gets enrolled, what the agents say, when a human takes over, and what it produces in pipeline. You set direction; the platform ops managers make it run. (Inbound request ops and routing sit with a colleague.)
Pipeline as your number, ROI as your story. Meetings booked → accepted → qualified pipeline created. Cost per meeting, cost per pipeline dollar. You report the program's return to leadership, with numbers that hold up under questioning.
The human SDR side. SDRs are the other half of the program - and where it most often breaks: lead quality disputes, unclear prioritization, follow-up that dies after one touch, handovers that lose context. You'll sit with the SDR teams and their leaders, find root causes, and fix them - with an AI assist, a process change, or a better definition.
The human–agent split. What agents do, what humans do, and where the handover sits. You own that line and move it based on evidence.
Signal-driven enrollment. Targeting runs on manual batches today. You'll drive the move to continuous enrollment based on account scoring, intent signals, and engagement decay. You define the logic; the ops team builds it.
The buying experience. Outreach should arrive because an account signalled something, say something true about the buyer's business, and make the next step obvious.
Program reporting. Volume, coverage, results, and ROI on a live dashboard, generated automatically. Parts still run on exports. Fix that early.
What comes next. The AI SDR pattern - signal in, agent acts, human closes - applies beyond outbound: event follow-up, hand-raiser nurture, re-engagement. Once the core program runs well, you'll make the case for the next one and drive its launch.
What success looks like after 3 months
Outbound volume and coverage are consistent across regions. Nobody asks "why did outbound drop last week?"
Leadership references your ROI model in planning: cost per meeting, cost per pipeline dollar, trend.
The top three SDR pain points from your first quarter are root-caused and fixed - and SDR leaders would confirm it unprompted.
Meeting acceptance is high. Rejections have known causes, not theories.
Reporting is fully automated. Your time goes into decisions.
The program activities and volume is connected to human activities, pipeline number for ICP accounts is bigger - and you can show which changes drove it.
At least one new agentic program is live and producing pipeline.

You've run programs with a number attached. Demand gen, SDR/BDR, growth, or GTM programs where you owned the outcome and defended the metric.
You've operated AI workflows in production. You've deployed, directed, or owned automations other people depended on. You can set requirements, challenge the build, and tell when the agent is the problem versus the data. You don't need to write code - you do need to never be bluffed by it.
ROI fluency. You can build a cost-per-outcome model and explain it. You'd rather show a live dashboard than a slide.
You diagnose team problems at the source. "The leads are bad" is where your investigation starts, not where it ends. You've worked with frontline teams, found the real constraint, and fixed it.
SDRs, AEs, and their leaders are your users. When the program misfires, you’ll be their point of contact.
The buyer's point of view. Buyers don't care that outreach was efficient - only that it was worth their time. You'll kill a volume that doesn't clear that bar.
Enough technical depth to be dangerous. You can read a workflow, question a data model, and learn a new tool in a week. Experience with our stack is welcome, not required.
Global comfort. Four regions, several languages, overlap with US hours.
Big Advantage:: hands-on LLM tooling beyond vendor UIs (Claude Code, MCP, custom agents); time in or working with SDR/BDR and demand gen function in B2B SaaS.
The stack you'll drive
Salesforce · Qualified · Salesloft · UserGems · Claude - plus a mandate to evaluate AI-native tooling with a clear bar for measurable impact.

You'll join Marketing Operations six people who operationalize and automate everything in marketing. Two of them work full-time on the AI SDR platform: they build and run it; you set its direction and co-own it: reporting and attribution, co-own and maintain inbound/outbound processes and find new tools. It's a team that builds its own tools rather than filing tickets for them.

A great deal of freedom and trust. At Bloomreach we don’t clock in and out, and we have neither corporate rules nor long approval processes. This freedom goes hand in hand with responsibility. We are interested in results from day one.
We have defined our 5 values and the 10 underlying key behaviors that we strongly believe in. We can only succeed if everyone lives these behaviors day to day. We've embedded them in our processes like recruitment, onboarding, feedback, personal development, performance review and internal communication.
We believe in flexible working hours to accommodate your working style.
We work virtual-first with several Bloomreach Hubs available across three continents.

Join the FIA and lead a pioneering safety technology programme.
As F1 Augmented Reality Project Manager within the FIA Technical Department, you will lead a strategic multi-year programme exploring how Augmented Reality and Head-Up Display technologies could enhance driver safety and situational awareness, particularly in conditions of reduced visibility.
You will act as the programme’s technical leader and systems integrator, coordinating specialised suppliers, research partners, Formula 1 teams and internal FIA stakeholders.
This is not a traditional project management role. It requires the technical knowledge to challenge engineering proposals, manage integration risks and drive complex technical decisions.
This new permanent, full-time position is based in Geneva.

Technical programme leadership
Define and own the multi-year technical roadmap, development phases, milestones and deliverables.
Structure the programme across key technologies, including helmet and visor displays, optical HUD solutions, sensors, vehicle positioning, data processing and sensor fusion.
Lead the programme from technology assessment and proof of concept through prototype development, integration and testing.
Maintain effective governance through risk, dependency, resource and milestone management.
Systems integration and technical coordination
Act as the technical systems integrator across on-car electronics, sensors, communication systems, data-processing solutions and driver equipment.
Translate safety and operational objectives into technical requirements, system architectures and validation plans.
Identify technical dependencies, interface constraints and integration risks across hardware and software systems.
Ensure that solutions address Formula 1 constraints, including packaging, weight, aerodynamics, cooling, latency, reliability and driver safety.
Supplier and stakeholder management
Identify and coordinate specialised technology suppliers, engineering partners and research organisations.
Review and challenge supplier proposals, technical architectures, test results, costs and delivery timelines.
Build alignment across Formula 1 teams, FIA technical departments, safety specialists and external partners.
Lead technical workshops, reconcile competing requirements and facilitate pragmatic compromises.
Testing, human factors and risk management
Coordinate simulation, laboratory evaluation, prototype development and vehicle-based testing.
Develop validation protocols for individual technologies and integrated solutions.
Assess human factors, including cognitive workload, visual ergonomics, information prioritisation, latency and emergency driver egress.
Identify and mitigate technical, safety, financial, intellectual property and programme-delivery risks.
Regulatory and strategic roadmap
Assess potential implications for FIA Technical, Sporting and Financial Regulations.
Support the development of regulatory, standardisation and implementation roadmaps.
